```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(cic)
```

## Start with a marker table

`out()` allocates a path; a writing function saves the contents. The examples run in a temporary directory, leave existing analysis results unchanged, and require neither Seurat nor real sequencing data.

```{r first-output}
result_dir <- tempfile("cic-guide-")
dir.create(result_dir)
markers <- data.frame(cell_type = c("T_cell", "B_cell"),
                      gene = c("CD3D", "MS4A1"))
path <- out("markers", ext = "csv", tag = "reviewed", dir = result_dir)
write.csv(markers, path, row.names = FALSE)
basename(path)
file.exists(path)
```

The name resembles `markers_reviewed_YYYYMMDD.csv`, using the date on which the example runs. In a real project, replace `result_dir` with your results directory.

## Handle existing filenames

The default `conflict = "ask"` presents a menu in interactive R and uses automatic numbering in non-interactive sessions. The example explicitly selects `"increment"` so it can run unattended:

```{r collision}
second <- out("markers", ext = "csv", tag = "reviewed", dir = result_dir,
              conflict = "increment")
write.csv(markers, second, row.names = FALSE)
basename(second)
stopifnot(path != second, file.exists(path), file.exists(second))
```

| Setting | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| `conflict = "ask"` | Default protection: interactive choice, automatic numbering in batch runs |
| `conflict = "increment"` | Choose an unused name ending in `_1`, `_2`, etc. |
| `conflict = "error"` | Stop on a collision so the calling workflow must handle it |
| `conflict = "overwrite"` | Explicitly allow the subsequent writer to overwrite the destination |

Use `timestamp = FALSE` to omit the date. `tag` accepts multiple tags; `ext` accepts an extension with or without a leading dot. A different existing extension raises an error instead of being silently replaced.

## Inspect logs {#logs}

```{r logs}
outputs(result_dir)[, c("action", "exists")]
outputs(result_dir, existing = TRUE, n = 1)[, c("action", "exists")]
```

The `.cic_outputs.csv` log is written when the path is allocated. This example allocates a path without saving data:

```{r pending}
pending <- out("not-written.rds", dir = result_dir, timestamp = FALSE)
outputs(result_dir, existing = FALSE)[, c("action", "exists")]
```

`exists = FALSE` can also mean that writing failed or a file was later deleted; it does not by itself prove a function failed. Logs contain `time, file, requested, action, script`, in that order. Existing non-empty logs are checked before appending. Malformed or incompatible logs raise an error; do not use an ordinary data CSV as a log file.

Disable logging per call with `log = FALSE`, or per project with `options(cic.out.log = FALSE)`. Logs contain absolute paths and possibly script names; review them before public sharing. `out()` does not provide a cross-process file lock.

## Save plots {#plots}

```{r plot, fig.show='hide'}
p <- ggplot2::ggplot(mtcars, ggplot2::aes(wt, mpg)) + ggplot2::geom_point()
figure <- ggsave1(file.path(result_dir, "scatter.pdf"), p, width = 5, height = 4)
stopifnot(file.exists(figure))
```

`ggsave1()` uses `out()` for path allocation and logging while retaining its existing arguments. `add_date = FALSE` omits the date; `confirm = FALSE` explicitly allows overwriting. These two arguments determine timestamp and collision handling independently of `cic.out.timestamp` and `cic.out.conflict`. Directory and logging options still apply.

## Configure a project

```{r project-options}
local({
  old <- options(cic.out.dir = result_dir, cic.out.timestamp = "%Y%m%d",
                 cic.out.conflict = "increment", cic.out.log = TRUE)
  on.exit(options(old))
  path <- out("summary.rds")
  saveRDS(markers, path)
  stopifnot(file.exists(path))
})
```

Explicit `out()` arguments override their corresponding options. Absolute paths are not relocated by `dir` or `cic.out.dir`. `create_dir = FALSE` requires the parent directory to exist. `outputs()` reads `cic.out.dir` by default, or the working directory when that option is unset; pass other directories explicitly. See `?out`, `?outputs` and `?ggsave1` for complete parameter documentation.

```{r cleanup, include=FALSE}
unlink(result_dir, recursive = TRUE)
```
